title: CC Payload
description: The document the core library writes to the compute store and the SDK reads at startup. Structure is taken from the embedded IOManager and Payload structs in USACE/cc-go-sdk payload.go. This is the contract shared by all four SDKs; conformance is proven by contracts/payload/.

attributes.description: Payload attributes: parameters the plugin reads to configure a run. Values may be string, number, boolean, array or nested object.
attributes.x-cc-known-divergence: The Confluence payload example and cc-home docs call this key 'payloadAttributes'. The Go struct tag says 'attributes'. An SDK that reads only 'payloadAttributes' silently sees an EMPTY attribute map against a Go-produced payload, and every {ATTR::} substitution then fails or resolves wrong. This is the single highest-value parity fixture in the suite: see contracts/payload/attributes-key-divergence/.

stores.description: DataStores reachable from this scope. cc-go-sdk connects each in order via connectStores() before substitution runs.
stores.x-cc-note: Present but empty in the minimal payload; cc-go-sdk's own testdata/test_payload.json has all four collections as empty arrays, so an SDK MUST NOT treat empty as absent.

inputs.description: Readable DataSources. Lookups search inputs then outputs when the caller does not specify INPUT/OUTPUT.

outputs.description: Writable DataSources. Put() and Copy() resolve their targets against OUTPUTS ONLY in cc-go-sdk, so writing to a name that exists only in inputs is an error even though the name is present in the payload.

actions.description: Ordered work items. Executed in array order; the same type may repeat; items may be omitted from a payload entirely.

x-cc-notes.required-fields-rationale: The four collections are required because cc-go-sdk unmarshals into typed slices and a missing key yields nil, which behaves identically to empty for every consumer. Requiring them makes the distinction explicit at the boundary without changing behavior. This is a NEW obligation and therefore a MAJOR contract change under STD-WIRE-002; it is recorded as proposed, not as current fact.
x-cc-notes.unknown-keys: additionalProperties: true is mandatory. STD-WIRE-003 requires unknown keys survive round-trip; a schema that rejects them would authorize SDKs to corrupt payloads written by a newer CLI.
x-cc-notes.no-version-field: The payload carries no version field today. An SDK therefore cannot know which contract revision a payload was written against. Adding one is proposed as 'contractVersion' (camelCase per STD-WIRE-005) and is a separate ADR.
